Resample and Tune Workflows on Start/Stop Survival Data

Source: R/tune_start_stop.R
tune_start_stop.Rd

Counterparts of [tune::fit_resamples()], [tune::tune_grid()] and [finetune::tune_race_anova()] for workflows whose outcome is `Surv(start, stop, event)`. Those functions cannot score start/stop data: the yardstick survival metrics need a right-censored truth, and tune scores each start/stop row as if it were a subject. Here each resample's assessment rows are collapsed to one row per subject with [collapse_start_stop_predictions()] before the metrics are computed, so every subject counts once and its survival follows its covariate path.

Usage

fit_resamples_start_stop(
  object,
  resamples,
  subject_id,
  metrics = NULL,
  eval_time = NULL,
  covariates = c("path", "baseline"),
  recurrent = c("error", "first"),
  trunc = 0.05,
  check_subject_overlap = TRUE,
  save_pred = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE
)

tune_grid_start_stop(
  object,
  resamples,
  subject_id,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  eval_time = NULL,
  covariates = c("path", "baseline"),
  recurrent = c("error", "first"),
  trunc = 0.05,
  check_subject_overlap = TRUE,
  save_pred = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE
)

tune_race_start_stop(
  object,
  resamples,
  subject_id,
  grid = 10,
  metrics = NULL,
  eval_time = NULL,
  covariates = c("path", "baseline"),
  recurrent = c("error", "first"),
  trunc = 0.05,
  check_subject_overlap = TRUE,
  save_pred = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  control = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A [workflows::workflow()] with a proportional-hazards model and a `Surv()` outcome.

resamples

An `rset`, grouped by subject.

subject_id

Name of the subject identifier column in the data.

metrics

A [yardstick::metric_set()] of survival metrics; defaults to the integrated Brier score and concordance. The first metric is the one `select_best()` and racing use by default.

eval_time

Evaluation times; defaults to deciles of the subjects' event times in the full data.

covariates, recurrent, trunc

As in [collapse_start_stop_predictions()].

check_subject_overlap

If `TRUE` (default), stop when a resample puts a subject in both its analysis and its assessment set.

save_pred

If `TRUE`, keep each resample's subject-level predictions in `.predictions`, for `tune::collect_predictions()`.

parallel

If `TRUE`, score resamples with [furrr::future_map()] (the burn-in resamples, when racing); set a [future::plan()] first.

grid

A data frame of candidate parameter values (columns named by the tuning parameters' ids), or a number of candidates for a space-filling design from [dials::grid_space_filling()].

control

For `tune_race_start_stop()`: a list or a [finetune::control_race()] object, of which `burn_in` (default 3), `alpha` (default 0.05) and `randomize` (default `TRUE`) are used.

Value

A `tune_results` object (class `start_stop_tune_results`) with `splits`, `id`, `.metrics`, `.notes` and, with `save_pred = TRUE`, `.predictions`.

Details

**Models.** The workflow's model must be [parsnip::proportional_hazards()] with the `"survival"` (coxph) or `"glmnet"` engine (from censored); both fit start/stop data, and scoring uses their linear predictor. Other censored-regression models either refuse start/stop outcomes or treat each row as a subject. With the glmnet engine, candidates that differ only in `penalty` share one fit per resample, as glmnet fits the whole path. Its `cox.ties` is set to `getOption("templecbe.cox_ties", "breslow")` unless the engine sets it, e.g. `set_engine("glmnet", cox.ties = "efron")`, which also silences glmnet 5.1's warning about the default tie handling. The pin is applied to an internal copy of the workflow, not to the workflow supplied: the workflow stored in the result (`tune::extract_workflow(res)`) carries the pin, so pass that workflow — not the workflow supplied here — to `tune::finalize_workflow()` when refitting the tuned model. Finalizing the supplied workflow refits without the pin, and so with glmnet's default tie handling.

**Resamples.** Group them by subject, e.g. [rsample::group_vfold_cv()] with `group = subject_id`, or [subject_vfold_cv()], which also stratifies the folds by each subject's event status. If a subject is in both the analysis and the assessment set of a resample, these functions stop before fitting (`check_subject_overlap = FALSE` skips the check). Out-of-bag sets of [rsample::group_bootstraps()] pass.

**Racing.** `tune_race_start_stop()` races the candidates with the rule of [finetune::tune_race_anova()]: after `burn_in` resamples, the first metric (at the first `eval_time` for a time-dependent metric) is modelled as `.estimate ~ candidate + resample`, and candidates whose `1 - alpha` confidence interval for the difference from the current best is entirely on the worse side are dropped. Eliminated candidates keep the metrics of the resamples they were scored on, and the attribute `race` lists every candidate with `n_resamples` and `eliminated`; `show_best()` and `select_best()` use the survivors, which are the candidates scored on every resample.

See also

[collapse_start_stop_predictions()], [cv_coxnet()], [nested_cv_coxnet()]

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("censored", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("workflows", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("tune", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("rsample", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:90, function(i) {
    k <- sample(1:3, 1)
    stops <- cumsum(stats::runif(k, 2, 6))
    risk <- stats::rnorm(1)
    data.frame(subject_id = i, tstart = c(0, utils::head(stops, -1)), tstop = stops,
               status = c(rep(0, k - 1), stats::rbinom(1, 1, stats::plogis(risk))),
               x1 = risk + stats::rnorm(k, sd = 0.2), x2 = stats::rnorm(k))
  }))
  spec <- parsnip::proportional_hazards(penalty = tune::tune(), mixture = 1) |>
    parsnip::set_engine("glmnet") |>
    parsnip::set_mode("censored regression")
  wflow <- workflows::workflow(survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, status) ~ x1 + x2, spec)
  folds <- rsample::group_vfold_cv(long, group = subject_id, v = 5)
  res <- tune_grid_start_stop(
    wflow, folds, subject_id = "subject_id",
    grid = data.frame(penalty = 10^seq(-3, -0.5, length.out = 8))
  )
  tune::show_best(res, metric = "brier_survival_integrated")
}
